text.en: Asha counted dozens of bananas and said, "Chemists count atoms in moles, just like we count in dozens."

Atoms are very small, so we compare their masses with the carbon-12 atom. Relative atomic mass is the ratio of the average mass of an atom of an element to one-twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom, and the average atomic mass is the weighted average over natural isotopes. A molecule is a discrete group of bonded atoms. Its relative molecular mass is the sum of the relative atomic masses of its atoms.
One mole of any substance contains 6.023 x 10^23 particles, which is Avogadro's number, and its mass in grams is the gram atomic mass or gram molecular mass. The number of moles = mass / molar mass. Percent composition tells the percentage by mass of each element in a compound.
In the ideal-gas model, equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of particles. If vapour density compares a gas with hydrogen gas at the same temperature and pressure, relative molecular mass is approximately twice this ratio.

problem.en: Find the amount and approximate number of molecules in 22 g of CO₂ (molar mass 44 g/mol).

text.en: Divide 22 by 44 to get 0.50 mol.

why.en: Grams divided by grams per mole gives moles.

text.en: Half of about 6.022 × 10²³ gives about 3.011 × 10²³ molecules.

why.en: Multiply the number of moles by the Avogadro constant.

problem.en: Estimate the mass percentage of oxygen in CO₂.

text.en: Oxygen contributes 2 × 16 = 32 out of a relative molecular mass of 44.

why.en: Count both oxygen atoms in the formula.
Mass percentage compares masses, not number of atoms.
